segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
36 when the combatants were stripped,
when the Armenians stripped them and left them plundered {OCR?},
and most of them were dissolved in the snow and died.
And afterward Bugha, the great general of the Tayyaye (Arabs), came and took Armenia captive,
and killed many in it.
And a little later, this same Bugha went against Zirak (Zayrak) the Turk who had rebelled in Tiflis,
and he killed the rebel by the Kur River, the one that passes through the midst of Tiflis.
And he set fire to the city,
and about fifty thousand human beings were burned in it.
And because all its buildings were of cedar wood,
which quickly catch fire and quickly extinguish,
and their embers do not endure like those of oak,
in one day they extinguished the fire again.
And the people of Homs again rebelled against the governor of the city and killed him.
At this time, when the Tayyaye saw
that it was a woman who was governing the empire of the Romans,
they despised them and broke the peace.
Then Queen Theodora sent an army of the Romans,
and it entered Cilicia in the year 1172 [AG],
1172 of the Greeks (801 to our Lord?):
and plundered the whole region of Anazarbus.
Now when al-Mutawakkil heard this,
he sent Nasif the eunuch to her on an embassy concerning peace and the redemption of captives.
She, however, replied: "We will make peace,
but from where do you have twenty thousand Christian captives,
so that you may give them in exchange for these Tayyaye who are with me?" Therefore, whatever the case,
when the eunuch enticed her with complete satisfaction {OCR?},
she released eight thousand,
and twelve thousand,
she said,
"These have been baptized and have become Christians;
it is not possible for us to give them up."
And it is said
that when this Nasif took these and departed,
Theodora killed them all,
because she saw that they were inclined to go out after they had believed and been baptized.
And others say
that Nicolaus, her own eunuch, killed them without the queen's command.
And in this same year, a people from among the Abyssinians who are called Beja went forth,
and killed all the Tayyaye who were working in the mines of gold and precious stones that were between the borders of Egypt and the Beja.
And a general of the Tayyaye named Anbasa went against them with twenty thousand horsemen and foot soldiers
